Description: The "Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, RTK2 subtype" is comprised of diffuse, astrocytic gliomas that are IDH-wildtype and H3-wildtype and have one or more of the following histological or genetic features: microvascular proliferation, necrosis, TERT promoter mutation, EGFR gene amplification, +7/−10 chromosome copy-number changes (CNS WHO grade 4). They also very commonly (~90%) harbor TP53 mutations and CDKN2A/B deletions (~70%). They can manifest in patients of any age but preferentially affects older adults, with peak incidence in patients aged 55–85 years. The RTK2 subtype harbours a higher frequency of EGFR amplification (~60%) than the RTK1 subtype. Expression profiles often resemble the 'Classical' subgroup according to the TCGA classification.
